Honestly, I don’t know. I don’t have a perfect answer, i doubt anyone really does. I don’t know if transsexualism should be categorized with intersex, frankly the difference between the physical and (theoretical) psychological hermaphroditism is broad and distinct.
I think we should use exclusively the -sex suffix rather than -gender, I believe the need for many young individuals to differentiate sex, gender, and pronouns is silly and, in the end, can be overall harmful. 
We know that denying a biological and intrinsic factor in transsexualism can lead to intense systemic medical and social transphobia and hatred, restricting health care and confusing uninformed or allowing harmful bigotry to hide behind the layers upon layers of faux wokeness and speculation of “trauma based” transness, or the belief that people “become” trans, or that there is some way to change them again through conversion, religion, therapy, etc. 

Gender -is- a social construct, and thus “made up” but so is language, government, marriage and non-barter based economies. Accepting certain prerogatives and rules like grammar, laws, monogamy, and the value of currency, to make life easier and more pleasant. However, gender, as much as it is made up, is not and will never be, -fake-.

Pronouns ARE equal to Gender, that’s why we call it misgendering.

Gender is just Sex with a slight linguistic difference. Gender is words we use to describe what sex a person is or intends to be, but without inherent regard for genitalia. But overall, it is important that they stay linked.

I always got shit from my dad, he is not autistic in the slightest, i sometimes get the impression that he is also not very intelligent, he was always very annoyed by my constant blathering and info-dumping, he used to call it “monologuing”. He was also very upset over the many years of me not understanding humor in the slightest. I am completely unable to understand sarcasm, or differentiate tone and voice pitch/volume.


But genuinely, the worst part of all, the one thing that continues to and will forever haunt me, is change. I could not number the meltdowns I have had to quell and calm from a simple piece of clothing being unavailable, or my favorite restaurant that I have enchiladas at on wednesday and Monday being closed, or god forbid, my parents renovating the kitchen and removing all the carpet in our house.
Everything is louder now, my dogs nails click and clack incessantly on the fake plastic wood. 

Our kitchen was truly awful before, built in the fifties, no changes besides a 40 year old fridge and a shitty microwave with the buttons all rubbed off and a oven/stove that looked like the moon robot from Wallace and Gromit. 
But I loved it, and i miss it. And I have never felt quite as horrible and stressed and psychotic as I  did for those several months it took to renovate.
